<title>Archive discipline: 3 shipped design plan(s) awaiting move to docs/archive/</title>
<description>
Weekly archive-discipline sweep, 2026-07-27, evaluated against `origin/main` @ `be1a7e99`.

Three design plans in `docs/design-plans/` have fully shipped and no longer gate active in-flight work. Per AGENTS.md and `docs/archive/README.md` they should move to `docs/archive/design-plans/` (with their test/implementation siblings, if any — none of these three have one).

**Do not just** `git mv` — each has inbound links that need updating in the same change.

---

## 1. `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-wallet-identity-durability.md`

All three phases Done:

| Phase | Issue | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| §2 Share 1 iCloud sync | <issue id="610c2d6d-2df5-4666-b0a6-c9ac603d1085" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-460/wallet-share-1-is-not-actually-icloud-synced-ksecattrsynchronizable-is">MM-460</issue> (Done 2026-07-25) | PR #426 · `307fd1be` |
| §3 Secure Enclave liveness probe | <issue id="6f6537a0-65d3-43a7-a4c3-5026a2c0aa51" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-461/wallet-secure-enclave-liveness-probe-dont-report-a-rotation-key-the">MM-461</issue> (Done 2026-07-26) | PR #448 · `da2cc5d0` |

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/linear-workflow

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

# Archive

Historical documents kept for the record — nothing in here describes the
current system authoritatively.

- **`design-plans/`, `test-plans/`, `implementation-plans/`** — dated plans
  whose work has fully landed (or was superseded). They are immutable
  historical records: when a plan's work ships and it stops being referenced

# Blobstore Resilience

**Status: survey + recommendations (2026-07-18). All five recommendations

section). The only follow-ons still open are the two wallet-side items noted in
the MM-434 section: the migration drain accepting the local iCloud mirror as a
*fallback blob source* (tracked as MM-446, whose iCloud-placeholder-download
dependency is MM-445), and `BGProcessingTask` background scheduling — polish on
top of the shipped resilience, not core durability.

# Wallet Identity Durability — Reinstall, Restore, and Redistribution

**Status: design, unstarted.** Tracked as MM-460 (§2), MM-461 (§3), MM-462 (§4).

Three defects in the wallet's local-persistence layer, found by auditing what actually
survives when the app's *installation* changes rather than when the *network* fails.
Each is small in code and large in consequence: the first
means the recovery model is one share weaker than designed, the second means the wallet
can claim custody it does not have, the third is a loaded footgun that has not fired yet.

This plan also writes down the thing that did not previously exist in one place: a
**durability matrix** stating, for every way an install can end, exactly what survives
and which recovery path applies. §1 is that matrix; §§2–4 are the three fixes; §5 maps
the seams to work already tracked elsewhere.

**Icebox / trigger-gated optimization — not actionable yet.** Filed for backlog visibility; revisit only when opted-in accounts show repo sizes large enough that [MM-447](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-447)'s full-CAR re-fetch on each pass becomes a real cost.

Design plan: `docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-22-wallet-repo-icloud-backup.md` §"Follow-ons under design discussion" (branch `claude/wallet-mst-repo-icloud-backup-3qe7wl`, PR #390). Archived under MM-485 — the plan's core and actionable follow-ons all shipped; this issue is the only remaining (On Ice) item.

## What

[MM-447](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-447) stores a **full-CAR snapshot**, re-fetched whole on each backup pass. This is the incremental alternative ("Option B"): store the repo as individual content-addressed IPLD blocks in iCloud, fetch only new blocks via `com.atproto.sync.getRepo?since=<rev>` (server-side incremental export already exists — [MM-184](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-184)), dedupe across snapshots, and **reassemble a CAR on-device** from the current commit root when an import/export is needed (via repo-engine's `collect_reachable_cids` + `build_car_from_cids`).

## Why deferred

The byte-heavy asset is blobs (backed up separately), so a repo-minus-blobs is typically a few MB; a full-CAR re-fetch is cheap and streamed. Option B adds a repo-engine dependency plus MST-walk and superseded-block-GC logic to the wallet to save bandwidth we don't meaningfully spend — complexity that only earns its keep at scale.

## Trigger to revisit

Real size data ([MM-447](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-447)'s status surface already shows snapshot size) showing that re-fetching the full CAR on each opportunistic/background pass is a meaningful battery/bandwidth cost. At that point the incremental model is justified.

content.text:
Done — [PR #463](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/463), MM-485 moved to In Review.

What landed:
- Three plans `git mv`'d into `docs/archive/design-plans/`.
- Inbound links repointed: [docs/blob-handling-spec.md:14](docs/blob-handling-spec.md:14), [docs/pds-architecture.md:55](docs/pds-architecture.md:55), [ADR-0030:6](docs/architecture/decisions/0030-stable-keychain-group-and-frozen-icloud-container.md:6), [2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md:249](docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md:249).
- One inbound reference the issue didn't list: the header comment in [scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh:18](scripts/bundle-identity-check.sh:18) also named the old path.
- Each plan's status header rewritten to record the landed state (the blobstore and repo-backup headers still asserted open follow-ons that have since shipped).
- MM-450's Linear description repointed to the archived path.
- `docs-check`, `changelog-check`, `ticket-ref-check`, `bundle-identity-check` all pass; every touched link target verified to resolve on disk.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The subtle failure mode in a doc move isn't the inbound links the issue enumerates — it's the **outbound** ones. `docs/design-plans/X.md` → `docs/archive/design-plans/X.md` adds a directory level, so every `../foo.md` inside the moved file silently starts resolving to `docs/archive/foo.md`. Only the blobstore plan had any (`../validation/`, `../blob-handling-spec.md`), re-based to `../../`.

This is also why `docs/archive/README.md` insists a design/test/implementation *triad* moves together: siblings at the same depth keep their relative cross-links intact for free, but splitting the triad breaks them in exactly this invisible way.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
